section_summary: The section begins with Japanese election materials: campaign finance reporting, voter registration, campaign publicity, absentee voting, candidate bulletins, and indexes to the two Diet election laws. Later documents report Chinese press criticism of Japan's occupation and economic recovery, a British editorial on Japan's new government, and a Japanese publicist's proposals for changing occupation policy. Several enclosures and clippings accompany diplomatic despatches.

subfiles.title: Election campaign income and disbursement form, concluding page
subfiles.about: The form records election income and disbursements.
subfiles.summary: Concluding instructions specify separate entries for income over 100 yen and detailed income categories.

subfiles.title: Law Concerning Special Registration Prior to Election
subfiles.about: Law No. 2 of 1947 establishes temporary registration for newly eligible voters.
subfiles.summary: The law permits supplementary electoral registers before the April 1947 elections and waives the usual six-month residence rule for repatriates voting in Diet elections. It also addresses local elections and repeals or amends earlier provisions.

subfiles.title: Home Ministry Ordinance No. 15 on Special Electors' Registers
subfiles.from: Etsujirō Uehara, Minister for Home Affairs
subfiles.about: The ordinance sets registration, inspection, objection, and confirmation dates for special electoral registers.
subfiles.summary: Sets March 1947 registration and review dates, with flexibility for districts where communication is difficult.

subfiles.title: Home Ministry Ordinance Extending National Election Registration Dates
subfiles.from: Etsujirō Uehara, Minister of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: The ordinance revises special register dates for the first postwar Diet elections.
subfiles.summary: Moves national election applications and register preparation into April, with confirmation scheduled for April 19.

subfiles.title: Law for Exceptions Concerning Writings, Drawings and Other Election Campaign Materials
subfiles.about: The law restricts printed campaign material during the 1947 elections.
subfiles.summary: Responding to shortages of paper and other materials, it limits postcards and posters, regulates newspaper advertisements and radio addresses, and sets penalties for violations.

subfiles.title: Excerpts from Ordinance Concerning Absentee Voting
subfiles.about: The excerpts describe eligibility and applications for absentee voting.
subfiles.summary: They cover seamen, railway workers, election workers, and people working away from home, including proof requirements and Braille requests.

subfiles.title: Excerpts from Ordinance Concerning Publication of Candidates' Names
subfiles.about: The excerpts govern candidate biographies and public postings for House of Councillors elections.
subfiles.summary: They specify submission, publication, distribution, and posting procedures, including word limits and drawing lots for candidate order.

subfiles.title: Index to House of Councillors Election Law
subfiles.about: An alphabetical subject index points to articles of the House of Councillors Election Law.
subfiles.summary: Lists article references for voting, candidacy, counting, campaign expenses, election officials, and penalties; page 213 repeats much of page 212.

subfiles.title: Index to House of Representatives Election Law
subfiles.about: An alphabetical subject index points to articles of the House of Representatives Election Law.
subfiles.summary: Lists article references for absentee voting, ballots, candidates, polling, campaign conduct, electoral registers, and offenses.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Shanghai Despatch
subfiles.about: A record copy replaces an unreturned action copy of a Shanghai despatch.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the substitute record copy for filing under 894.00/5-2647.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Chinese Reception of “Japan Purges First Families”
subfiles.from: Fred W. Connors, for the Consul General at Shanghai
subfiles.about: The despatch reports Chinese newspaper use of a U.S. information article and criticism of Japan policy.
subfiles.summary: It estimates that 22 Chinese newspapers carried the article and describes critical editorials, fears of renewed Japanese aggression, and resistance to an early peace treaty. It encloses an editorial and a Central News Agency report.

subfiles.title: “There Must Be a Democratic Japan”
subfiles.about: The editorial warns that Japanese reactionaries threaten future peace.
subfiles.summary: It criticizes MacArthur's support for conservatives and the Yoshida Cabinet, recalls Chinese suffering under Japan, and argues that only a democratic Japan can prevent another war.

subfiles.title: Central News Agency Report on Japan's Economic Future
subfiles.about: The report argues that a peace treaty could restore Japan's regional economic dominance.
subfiles.summary: It alleges that Japanese claims of food shortages and unreliable economic statistics are shaping occupation policy. It questions plans to rebuild Japan as Asia's industrial center.

subfiles.title: London Despatch Transmitting The Times Editorial “Japan New and Old”
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, for the Ambassador in London
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards an editorial on political change and continuing Allied control in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the May 27 Times editorial and summarizes its concern that democratic changes have barely touched Japanese life.

subfiles.title: “Japan New and Old”
subfiles.about: The editorial assesses Katayama's government and argues for continued Allied oversight.
subfiles.summary: The article examines Tetsu Katayama's difficult coalition prospects after the election and questions how deeply democratic reforms have changed Japanese political habits. It supports economic survival while warning that premature withdrawal of Allied control could permit renewed aggression. The clipping is reproduced repeatedly across these pages.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Tokyo Despatch
subfiles.about: A record copy replaces an unreturned action copy of a Tokyo despatch.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the substitute record copy for filing under 894.00/6-547.

subfiles.title: Despatch Transmitting Tetsuma Hashimoto's Memorandum
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a Japanese publicist's views on Allied and American occupation policies.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Hashimoto's memorandum, his covering letter, and a Tokyo police report about him.

subfiles.title: Summary Translation of Tetsuma Hashimoto's Memorandum
subfiles.about: Hashimoto proposes a moral and economic reappraisal of the occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hashimoto argues that victors and defeated nations share responsibility for war and that lasting peace requires mutual understanding rather than punishment. He criticizes reparations, trade restrictions, industrial controls, broad purges, and policies he believes undermine Japanese traditions. He urges economic assistance and warns that hardship and political polarization could revive extremism; the memorandum continues beyond page 241.
